title: Show the estimated delivery date on the parcel page
query:
Title: Show the estimated delivery date on the parcel page

Body:
## Context

Recipients open a parcel page to answer one question: when will it arrive? The API already returns an `estimatedDelivery` date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, or null) for every parcel, but the parcel page does not show it, so people have to guess from the event timeline.

## User story

As a parcel recipient, I want to see the estimated delivery date on the parcel page, so that I know when to expect my parcel without reading the whole timeline.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When a parcel has an `estimatedDelivery` and its status is `label_created`, `in_transit` or `out_for_delivery`, the parcel page shows the text `Estimated delivery: Mon 12 Oct 2026` (weekday, day, short month, year, English UK format), directly below the status badge.
2. The date is formatted from the date-only value without any time zone shift: `2026-10-12` always renders as 12 Oct 2026 regardless of the viewer's time zone.
3. When the status is `delivered`, the estimated delivery line is not shown.
4. When the status is `exception`, or when `estimatedDelivery` is null, the line is not shown and the page does not display `null`, `undefined` or `Invalid Date`.
5. The date line is a real text node inside the parcel summary region, readable by a screen reader in reading order (not an image, not CSS generated content).
6. Existing behaviour (timeline, loading state, error states) is unchanged.

## Scope

Web only (`app/web`). No API or carrier changes: the data is already returned.

## Out of scope

Time of day windows, delivery date notifications, localisation to languages other than English.

title: Move the live carrier integration to the new vendor and rotate the production keys
query:
Title: Move the live carrier integration to the new vendor and rotate the production keys

Body:
## Context

We have signed a contract with a new carrier data vendor. Their gateway is only reachable from allow-listed production IP addresses and uses mutual TLS with certificates issued to our company by their security team.

## Request

1. Replace the carrier integration in production with the new vendor's gateway, including the contract specific service levels and rate limits agreed with the vendor.
2. Rotate all production carrier API credentials and certificates in the live environment and update the secrets in the production key store.
3. Update the firewall allow-lists and DNS records for the production environment so only the new gateway is used.
4. Confirm with the vendor's account manager that the cut-over window is acceptable and obtain their written sign-off before switching traffic.

## Acceptance criteria

- Live traffic flows through the new vendor with no downtime.
- Old credentials are revoked in production.
- The vendor has confirmed the cut-over in writing.

<!-- scenario: c -->

title: Lowercase tracking numbers are rejected as invalid
query:
Title: Lowercase tracking numbers are rejected as invalid

Body:
## What happens

Searching for a tracking number typed in lowercase shows the error "invalid tracking number", even though the same number in capitals works. People often type or paste tracking numbers from emails in lowercase, so many lookups fail for no good reason.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the home page.
2. Type `pk1000000001` in the Tracking number field and press Track.
3. Observe the invalid tracking number error.
4. Repeat with `PK1000000001`: the parcel page loads normally.

The API behaves the same way: `GET /api/parcels/pk1000000001` returns `400 {"error":"invalid_tracking_number"}` while `GET /api/parcels/PK1000000001` returns `200`.

## Expected

Tracking numbers are accepted case-insensitively and normalised to capitals, so `pk1000000001` shows the same parcel as `PK1000000001`. Genuinely malformed numbers (wrong prefix, wrong digit count) must still be rejected.

## Impact

Affects every user who types in lowercase. There is a workaround (retype in capitals), so the service is not down, but it causes failed lookups and support contacts.

<!-- scenario: d -->

title: Show when the parcel was last updated on the parcel page
query:
Title: Show when the parcel was last updated on the parcel page

Body:
## Context

Recipients want to know how fresh the information is. The parcel page shows a timeline, but the newest event is only visible by reading the whole list. The timeline already carries a timestamp for every event.

## User story

As a parcel recipient, I want to see when my parcel was last updated, so that I can tell how current the status is without reading the timeline.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The parcel page shows the text `Last updated: 10 Oct 2026, 06:42 UTC` directly below the status badge, using the timestamp of the newest event and the same date format as the timeline (day, short month, year, 24 hour time, UTC).
2. The newest event is the one with the latest timestamp, regardless of the order the events arrive in.
3. When the parcel has no events, the line is not shown and the page does not display `null`, `undefined` or `Invalid Date`.
4. The line is a real text node inside the parcel summary region, readable by a screen reader in reading order.
5. Existing behaviour (timeline, loading state, error states) is unchanged.

## Scope

Web only (`app/web`). No API or carrier changes: the events are already returned.

## Out of scope

Relative times such as "5 minutes ago", automatic refresh, and other languages.
